scene.note: Some of your functions change the board everyone reads, and some hand back a new plan and leave the board alone.

steps.note: Ailsa asks what the board would look like with one more square.
The function gets the board itself, under a second name, so it must not change it.
A new list comes back with the square at the end, and the board stays as it was.
A team radios in: one square is done.
The square comes off the board itself, if it is there, and nothing comes back.
Every team reading the board sees it gone.
Ailsa wants a draft order for the next team, starting with one square.
The changes happen on a copy, never on the board.
The draft comes back with that square first, and the board keeps its order.
At the end of a shift, several squares are done, some of them side by side.
The loop goes through something that does not change, so it never skips a square.
Every searched square comes off the board itself.
